Plain Text Files
Part 2: Reading,
Writing, and
Appending to Files
Files can be accessed and altered in
Python with reading, writing, and
appending.

Reading, Writing, and Appending
Python can open text files in different modes
depending on what you want to do.
"r" (read mode) reads an existing file without
changing it.
"w" (write mode) writes to a file and replaces any
existing contents.
"a" (append mode) adds new content to the end of
an existing file.

Code Example of Reading, Processing, and Writing a File
with open("students.txt", "r") as file:
students = file.readlines()
processed_students = []
for student in students:
student = student.strip().title()
processed_students.append(student)
with open("students.txt", "w") as file:
for student in processed_students:
file.write(student + "\n")
